newsitem.title: UK: Siebe extends bounce in wake of results.
newsitem.headline: Siebe extends bounce in wake of results.

text.p: Shares in international engineering group Siebe Plc rose for the second day in a row on Wednesday, as brokers BZW reiterated a buy recommendation in the wake of robust results, traders said.
Siebe, which reported a 32 percent rise in first-half profits on Tuesday, saw its shares rise to a high of 969.75p. But by 1220 GMT, the stock had stabilised at 959.5p, up 9.5p.

Traders said BZW believed Siebe to have excellent long-term growth prospects and to be resilient to mixed markets, managing to achieve 25 percent earnings growth. Underlying trade going forward was stronger than BZW had expected, traders noted.

Siebe's shares have been on a rising trend since February 1995, doubling to peak at 1007.5 pence at the end of September 1996. But since then, they have dipped to 940 pence, only picking up again two days ago on stronger-than-expected results.
Following today's jump in shares, Siebe's stock has outperformed the FTSE all-share index by almost 13.7 percent over the last 12 months, according to Reuters graphics.
